traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), families 372 Liliaceae (the asphodels, onions and hyacinths), Amaryllidaceae, 386 Iridaceae and 405 Orchidaceae, the bulk of APG's Asparagales: perianth of six petal-like segments in two whorls of three; an orchid's are unlike (its lip), which its family states.

traits.flowering_position.note: Wikipedia Asparagales (read 2026-10-16): flowers often clustered at the stem tip; scapes of the geophytes end their shoots. Orchidaceae (which would outweigh this) gets its own value; this weighting is for the families outside it.

traits.inflorescence.note: Inferred weighting: racemes in Scilloideae, Asphodelaceae and most orchids; panicles in Agave, Yucca; umbels in Amaryllidaceae (which states its own). Asparagaceae is the main family inheriting it.

traits.sexual_system.note: DELTA Orchidaceae (read 2026-10-16) and family states: flowers bisexual through nearly all of the order; dioecy only in some Asparagus, Ruscus and Asteliaceae.

traits.hypanthium.note: Wikipedia Asparagales (read 2026-10-16): tepals free or joined at base; a floral tube or cup occurs in some Amaryllidaceae and Iridaceae, which state it themselves.

traits.rosette.note: Wikipedia Asparagales (read 2026-10-16): most species have a basal or terminal leaf rosette, a few have leaves along the stem.

traits.zygomorphy.note: APweb Asparagales page (read 2026-10-16): orchids strongly monosymmetric with a labellum from the inner whorl; Orchidaceae (about 28,000 spp.) sets 'usually'. Other zygomorphic flowers (Amaryllidaceae, Asphodelaceae) overridden to other.
